I love Audiosurf, want to get fit, and have a passionate hatred towards orbs - this is excellent! :D
This feels like swimming through your music, punching evil jellyfishes in bass-fueled FURY, it is wonderful! :D

Like with Audiosurf, to have the most fun, you have to take the time to git gud (that's a good thing), and all the way from starting out at Normal (easy) to becoming 'one with the game', and shredding the craziest patterns on Elite, this is a proper sport! You WILL get soaked in sweat, and you WILL feel ALIVE!
Who knew the best motivator to exercise was video games!? :D
(video on Steam shows 'medium' difficulty by the way, it gets way more intense!)

[h2]Important technical tips[/h2]
[b]Sync[/b]
Oddly, "Audioshield (literally) puts YOU (fail) at the point of impact", NOT your shields (win) - this is why some people complain about music sync being 'off' - the game doesn't account for you extending your arms (wtf).
The solution here is very simple: You can effectively adjust the sync by standing ahead or behind the foot markings on the floor.
Standing just behind the marking, with my toes almost touching the marked heels is what works best for me - the orbs become perfectly synced with the moves, awesome! :D

[b]Orb height[/b]
Audioshield calibrates to your height just after the level loading screen, or when you pause-unpause! If you get orbs uncomfortably low, it's probably because you leaned down to scratch your leg at the wrong moment - pause-unpause while standing tall to fix it!

[b]Level generation[/b]
The orbs may be synced to a different instrument than you expect - adequate(-ly tuned) audio equipment and higher volume will quickly make it obvious. It'll sync to vocals too, which actually works surprisingly well!

[h2]Concept & main gameplay: 10/10![/h2]
I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game! It is wonderful fun, AND keeps you feeling alive, blood pumping! Never regretted getting out of the chair and putting on the old Vive for this!
[h2]The 'supporting elements': 6/10[/h2]
There is nothing game-breakingly wrong here, however, here's a little wishlist of improvements:
[list]
[*][b]Song browser menu SUCKS![/b] (it's the same as Audiosurf 2)
I have a folder of ~250 songs, and I refuse to add navigational steps by organizing them into folders - a huge alphabetical list works great for me everywhere but here! The song entries are huge, all unnecessarily showing the song's cover art (which lags the game to load), AND there's no scroll handle, so you're stuck scrolling up/down at a pace much slower than what you could do otherwise.
This is a lot of text for something relatively minor, but man, I HATE UI which cannot keep up with my intentions!
[*][b]Dead time between the action[/b]
Sure, you need a little moment to get into position after clicking 'Start', and the first orbs arriving, but nowhere near as much as the game gives you. After the song ends, too - sure, it's nice to get a little extra moment in-world, rather than jumping to the leaderboard immediately after the last note, but it hangs on just a little too long.
I understand why some may prefer these timings the way they are, but this should be adjustable in the settings.

Really it's not too-too bad, and the game does at least load quickly!

Another way to reduce overall 'dead time' would of course be to improve the song browser, but besides that, I'd love to see these simple additions immediately to the leaderboard section, the following options: 'Play next song in folder', 'Play (randomly selected song)', and 'Re-roll random song'.
The random selection stuff would help with moments of indecision, too :)
[*][b]Leaderboards[/b]
I'd like to see results from other modes on the leaderboards - I wouldn't mind downgrading difficulty level, or switching to/from fitness mode, if it meant I had someone to play against for an obscure (or new) song, if only there was a way to know!
Playing obscure music in a relatively obscure game, on kinda obscure hardware, finding people on boards needs all the help it can get! (Still, more-popular music is surprisingly well populated with results!).

A possible solution would be to show results from all 3 main difficulty levels on one board, but base the order on an extra number - a 'difficulty-adjusted combined score', where you'd get 100k knocked off the score for every level below Elite. This could be an option for all boards, or could be automatically applied to all songs with only a few results total.
To avoid making things too messy, mode icons could be displayed (optionally instead of avatars), or entry backgrounds/text could be color-coded.

It would also be nice to see timestamps of peoples' results! In Audiosurf (1), it is very satisfying to beat long-standing records, and it's great to see recent competition popping up! Would be nice to have that here, too!
[*][b]Height calibration[/b]
This is kinda minor, but I'm not a fan of making sure to stand tall at the right time every time the game loads. An option to permanently set your height would be nice - just add a dedicated 'set height' button to the intro screen/pause menu, and it'll all be great!
Sure, it's more 'seamless' to have it adjusted without the user knowing at all, but I see this automation causing more trouble than it's worth.
[*][b]Steam features[/b]
Steam achievements are a lot of fun, but the game has none! I'd love some overarching goals besides dominating all the leaderboards!

Steam Workshop! Audioshield is just as moddable as Audiosurf 2 (very!), and I really don't understand why there's no Steam Workshop support! Personally, I'm not super keen on segmenting the leaderboards with modes even more, but still, I'm sure there are people with very creative gameplay ideas, just no good place to share them!

I'd also love to see some custom skins for this! The base game has a good selection of them, but I'd love to see more, especially with interesting dynamic elements!
Coming from Audiosurf, one thing I'm missing here is the sense of environmental exploration - it was very interesting to see what track shapes the game came up with. Dancing in place instead of riding a vehicle, you understandably lose this element, but I'm sure custom skins could bring some of that magic back in one way or another! :)
[*][b]Better fitness mode[/b]
Fitness mode can work great, but only one extra move (ducking) gets repetitive. More interesting stuff could be done!
Jumping, leaning side-to-side, perhaps something to avoid with your hands (but ok to touch with head). Hell, perhaps move/rotate the fighting position itself and make the user change position entirely - make some use of bigger playspaces!
Regarding how things currently are, my biggest gripe with fitness mode is how calmer songs can force you to basically sit on the floor for a while. It's just awkward.
[/list]
[h2]In the end[/h2]
Sure, I talked mostly about what could be improved, and how to make the most of the game, but rest assured, Audioshield is totally AWESOME!
I just cannot come up with more combinations of words to describe the sheer fun of playing this thing! :D

Don't buy it on sale, buy it for full price, the raw entertainment here is absolutely worth it, and the dev deserves it, alongside the encouragement to polish this solid 9/10 game over the edge to 10/10!

By the way, if you're reading this and don't own VR kit, I'd say that this game alone makes it worth getting your hands on! You can get an original Vive (full kit) used for $100-$200 now, and Audioshield runs great even on hardware below minimum VR spec (FX-6300@4.7, Fury X, Windows 7 here).

Got a music library of MP3s or FLACs? Or maybe a bunch of Special Edition soundtracks kicking around on Steam? (We both know the answer to that last question.) If so, you'll love this game. I've been playing it for 40 minutes during my lunch break every weekday for months now after getting back into VR. It's the only VR game I play with any consistency at this point.

I keep coming back to it for a couple reasons:
[list]
[*]No matter how obscure, you can play any song as long as you have the file. You can even play stuff you make, if you're musically inclined.
[*]This game really gets you moving. The right song on the higher difficulties can be amazingly brutal, especially if you really get into it. You'll start seeing note placements that look impossible but become so, so satisfying when you learn how to nail them without chucking your controller.
[*]The color, type and relative placement of "notes" are somewhat different every time -- that's by design (and I believe there's a mod out there that lets you disable it, if you're so inclined). You can get a good feel for the general pacing, but execution is on the fly. IMO this is a good thing, as it lets you keep revisiting the real bangers without getting bored of them.
[*]It's intuitive and elemental. Put it on the black background and crank the difficulty, and it's just you and the song. I actually have to set an external timer to bring me back from full-on goblin mode.
[/list]

You might see some reviews here and there talking about inconsistent mapping. From my experience that's based on two things: the difficulty (Expert seems to get the closest) and the song file itself -- the algorithm is looking for contrast to define where "notes" are and establish timing, so if your track is just a mess of mids with some highs, it's going to pick the highs out more consistently than the mids and may miss stuff. Means some genres really shine, and songs with poor mixing (and certain live albums) don't fare as well. But the way it reads the song also leads to some really, really cool interactions with stuff it likes that's produced cleanly. E/IDM and electronica are absolutely killer, as is pop and prog. Metal gets a bit iffy depending on the artist and album.


Still reading? Well, if you pick up this game, get North Circular by Squarepusher (it's a track from "Feed Me Weird Things" and should cost you a buck). Put it on Expert (don't worry, you won't flunk out like in Guitar Hero) and just watch for what happens at around 1:10. It's a great example of what you can find exploring songs. Also, if you have the Furi soundtrack, you owe it to yourself to play it.

I'd had my eyes on Audio Shield for a long time, it was actually the first rhythm VR game I ever wishlisted. I loved the idea of adding my own music. Well I finally got the game and fired it up today. It took a second to figure out how to add my music to the game. Once I did though I couldn't stop for almost an hour!

I finally got to play The Stupendium's song Impossible Geometry... a song about Beat Saber... in a rhythm game! I actually played a bunch of Stupendium's music and it was an absolute blast. Highly recommend that music in this game.

So obviously I like the game... but here's some notes...

1) About Adding Your Music: You do have to have the mp4 files on your pc in order to add the music to your game. Be it with files you've had on your pc for a while... or even soundtracks from steam (I'm gonna play the hell out of Skul's Soundtrack ngl). It's really easy to do. From within the game you can go to whatever drive your music is on, go to the folder, and then select the song. Once you select the song you get to select difficulty, background, type of shield, and then you are off to the races! The game will auto generate a map for your song to whatever difficulty you selected and the maps are pretty damn good. The only way the music situation can make this game suck for you is if you are the kind of person who has only ever listened to music on Spotify.

2) About the Maps: Like I said the maps are really good for being Auto Generated. There is the occasional moment where two different color notes are immediately one after the other, in the same spot, and it's damn impossible to hit. Otherwise they are really good maps. A word of caution though, your first play through of a song may be a bit laggy. The game generates the maps pretty quickly, but once you load in for the first time that song can be a bit wonky. Once you've played it that first time though it plays seamlessly. You can also save a song to favorites if you enjoyed it so you don't have to hunt the song down again. I will say that the beats seem to be kinda off on Normal maps, but once you pump up to hard the maps are pretty good at matching the beat. Honestly the normal ones only seem off cause they have fewer notes.

3) The Youtube Situation: This is a non issue for me but I figured I would address it. I understand that people who purchased the game when it had the Youtube support were upset when the game had this feature removed. I understand it and it is justifiable if you bought the game for that reason. However, to  me, this does not reduce the quality of the game in the slightest. Like I said.. if you have an actual copy of a song on your computer... you can play it! There's no limit on how much music you can play. There's no modding involved to play a song you like. You can play whatever song you want... and they won't even be sensored *le gasp*. Seriously, there not being youtube only ruins the game if you don't have any mp3s on your pc or on a jumpdrive somewhere. As someone who never got rid of her files from her MP3 player from "ye days of old" I've got a ton of music to play. As someone who still owns CD's from "ye days of old" I can rip whatever music I want onto my pc and play it freely. As someone who owns soundtracks for various games on her account. Let's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ go! So seriously. If you fall into the category of "Person who has the abilty to get or who has mp3 files" you can play and enjoy this game.

4) Graphics: Omg I love them. You have a selection of a few backgrounds to play on and there's nothing "spectacular" about any of them, but they are nice. Where the graphics are really cool in this game is that when you first start the game... way off in the distance.... you can see tons of little dots of red and blue. Those are your notes... coming at your face. It's honestly really cool to be able to see just how many notes are going to be coming your way as you play. They don't show up a few seconds before you hit them. Nah nah nah. You get the full scope of what you will be doing almost right out of the gate. A few songs I played I saw those dots in the distance and was like "Oh ♥♥♥♥ I'm about to get wrecked..."

5) Controls: The controls are simple. You have shields on your hands and you smack the orbs. Put hands together to smack purple notes. If you wanna get some extra movement in and get some aggression out then feel free to punch them. Simple mechanic. The only thing is that it seems like if your shields aren't somewhat within your FOV that you will miss notes which is kinda annoying. You also can't move much. There is an area highlight that you have to stay in and if you move out of that little square you will miss tons of notes. Not really a control here, but a mechanic. You don't seem to be able to "fail" a song. Which is something I really like as it means I can just play and enjoy the song. I won't have my song suddenly ended because I missed a few notes. At the end you see how well you did and it's just kinda all about beating yourself and your high score. So it's not about failing, it's about how good you did.

6) Difficulty: It really depends on the song. I found some of the songs I played were super easy on normal... and not awful on hard... but some songs just kicked my ass in hard difficulty. Which I loved :) tbh

7) Exercise: Omg this is a work out! There is ALOT more full body movement in this than Beat Saber as the notes fly in from a pretty wide FOV. Notes can also come from slightly above you so you have to look up to hit them and then look back down to hit more. It's not rapid head movement, but head movement. The wide FOV makes it so you have to look around and move your body around more. If you decide to actually punch notes rather than just gently tapping them it adds even more to the work out. 

Conclusion: This is a damn good game and highly underrated. Again the amount of music you can play is limitless. Even more so than modding because with modding YOU have to make your map or hope someone else has. With this game you can play whatever you can get your hands on easily. It's far more of a work out than any other rhythm VR game I've played so far. It can be a bit laggy at points but by far this does not make the game unplayable by any means. The only real downside I could think of is that it takes like 30 seconds to load a song in for the first time... so when you first start playing you need a bit of patience. Once you have a library of maps built up though you'll be golden.
